non_claims: Does not remove the need for R1 and R3: ErasureAgrees itself fails for ghost writes to real state (2.1), diverging ghost code (2.3), and failing ghost assertions (2.4).

erase P is again a Stmt run on a full Store. For R2-violating programs, erase P still reads ghost variables (erase (x := g) = x := g) and executes at all only because of this encoding; a compiler targeting real stores would reject it. Under R2 the erased program ignores the ghost part of its store (erase_rbehaves_congr_of_realReadsReal).

Toy model, and R1, R2, R3a, R3b are not shown sufficient for sound ghost erasure in richer languages or verifiers: deterministic sequential while-language with only inhabited Int variables, total expressions (Expr.eval cannot fail or diverge), fatal uncatchable assert failure, no procedures or recursion (a ghost lemma call is an inline ghost block), no heap, no ghost fields, no ghost functions inside specifications, no nondeterministic choice, no concurrency. It does not address empty or uninhabited ghost types (witness checks), assume statements or unverified axioms, witnessless existential choice, mutable heap aliasing between ghost and real references, catchable exceptions or early exits (return, break) escaping a ghost block, or concurrent interleavings. Transfer to Dafny or Why3 is a modeling bridge, not a kernel-checked fact.
